summary.headline: Sharda Motor's value-added sales grew 27% YoY in Q2 FY27, ahead of ~20% gross profit growth; exports have yet to start.
summary.overview: Management said value-added sales grew 27% YoY in Q2 FY27, ahead of gross profit growth of about 20%, driven by emission-segment volumes and new light-weighting programs that entered SOP. Start-up costs, product mix and non-index commodity inflation weighed on margins. The Hyundai production-loss recovery and premium freight normalisation from Q1 are largely complete. Export orders (about 17.8 million peak annual value, about 94 million lifetime) have been announced but have not yet started shipping. The transcript is garbled in places, and the consolidated revenue figure is not legible, so the top-line and margin numbers could not be verified from the call.

financial_highlights.change: Higher than usual vs. prior pattern, per management

financial_highlights.metric: Value-added sales absolute numbers, with and without catalysts

segments.name: Emission systems
segments.commentary: Existing emission vertical contributed to the 27% value-added sales growth in Q2; management also sees the emission business moving from BS6 to WLTP and then VS7/CAFE, with WLTP content-per-vehicle uplift described as marginal.

segments.name: Light-weighting (control arms, subframes)
segments.commentary: New programs have gone into SOP and are contributing to growth but are still ramping with start-up costs; control arm RFQ won with Dongi partnership and will be delivered from the existing facility, while subframe winning would need a new facility or KPIX.

segments.name: Exhaust (premium higher-CC motorcycles)
segments.commentary: Company won a two-year exhaust order in the premium higher-CC motorcycle segment this quarter; management is prioritising execution with incremental capex, and scooters/other two-wheeler segments were not confirmed as targets.

segments.name: Exports (genset and agri-equipment)
segments.commentary: Orders announced worth about 17.8 million peak annual business value (about 94 million lifetime) across three segments: North American genset maker, a leading North American agriculture equipment OEM, and a large heavy-industry emission customer; export revenue has not yet started.

guidance_outlook: North American genset SOPs were on track to start in Q3 FY27, with the customer confirming no postponement despite US EPA norm uncertainty.
Customer ramp-up to peak annual value is typically 1.5 to 2 years after SOP, varying by project.
Management would not give a timeline for acquisitions; it is evaluating targets that must be value-accretive, technologically suitable and integratable.
Management declined to comment on buyback; capital allocation to be decided by the board and dividend policy continues to be followed.
Euro 7 product under development with one OEM for exports; BS7 joint development is underway.
capex_capacity: Subframe RFQ wins would require new facility or KPIX setup, with manufacturing built during the delivery timeline and Dongi supporting process and design.
Premium motorcycle exhaust orders to be served using existing manufacturing setup, R&D and system engineering with incremental capex only.
Management says it expects to work with OEM expansion plans and follow customers to new locations, but did not disclose any specific plant plans.
Chennai R&D centre cited; 26 patents filed and 6 granted.
demand_pricing: Management described Indian automobile production growth of 18.6% YoY in Q2 FY27, with passenger vehicle production up 8.9% and special vehicles up 33.9%, although the figures were partly garbled in the transcript.
Non-index commodity costs moved adversely over the last few months, which had a marginal impact on Q2 results.
Premium raw material and freight costs are normalising, but consumables, BOPs and inward freight remain a drag, which management is offsetting through efficiencies and customer negotiations.
Pass-through catalyst revenue is customer-directed; management would not disclose with/without-catalyst figures and said value-added numbers would be shared later.
Export RFQ traction is good across the targeted segments, and existing customers are giving incremental orders.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the 27% value-added sales growth is quantified, and why did gross profit grow only ~20%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management did not quantify value-added sales in rupee terms. The gap versus gross profit reflects SOP start-up costs on new light-weighting programs, product mix and non-index commodity costs; export contribution has not yet started.

qa_highlights.question: Are the North American genset SOPs on track for Q3 FY27, given EPA norm uncertainty?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes. Management said it is in the middle of Q3 FY27 and on track, with the customer confirming no delay or postponement, and the orders are not all tied to EPA norms.

qa_highlights.question: Does the company have high-tensile steel and aluminium capability for control arms?
qa_highlights.answer: Light-weighting control arms rely on high-tensile steel stamping plus Dongi's design, process and assembly know-how; management said a separate detailed discussion would follow.

qa_highlights.question: Will WLTP and emission upgrades raise content per vehicle and share of business?
qa_highlights.answer: Content-per-vehicle impact is marginal. Share of business is an OEM decision. Management relies on local R&D and an upgrade path toward VS7/CAFE.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a timeline for acquisitions, and is a buyback under consideration?
qa_highlights.answer: No timeline was given; targets must be value-accretive, technologically right and integratable. On buyback, management said nothing could be commented on yet, with the board to decide and dividend policy followed.

qa_highlights.question: Has the Hyundai production-loss recovery and premium freight issue normalised?
qa_highlights.answer: The customer has largely recovered from the Q1 production loss, giving a small positive in Q2. Premium freight has largely normalised, but other non-index cost items remain.

qa_highlights.question: Is the company on the hybrid and multi-fuel platform, and what are the next steps for subframe RFQs?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes; orders already exist across CNG, hybrid, diesel and petrol. The control arm is already won with Dongi; subframe wins would need a KPIX and new facility.

risks_watch: Gross profit growth (~20%) lagging value-added sales growth (27%) due to SOP start-up costs and non-index commodity inflation.
Start-up of two North American genset SOPs in Q3 FY27 and any future EPA-related delay.
Export revenue start-up timing and conversion of the RFQ pipeline into orders.
Undisclosed catalyst pass-through and with/without-catalyst revenue numbers limit visibility into underlying growth.
Acquisition and capital-allocation plans remain open; no timeline or buyback decision provided.
summary.management_tone: Confident on demand, order wins and SOP timelines, but guarded on quantification: management repeatedly declined to give rupee value-added, catalyst, buyback and acquisition-timeline details, citing confidentiality or the need to decide later.
key_quotes: So we are right now in the middle as it started.
We are fully on target in Q3 FY27.
There is demand. Our strategy of exports is playing out fairly well.

rows.when: Q3 FY27 onward; peak 1.5-2 years after SOP
